data.narrative:
Freeform, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Erik Palitsch, has raised $125M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector comparables: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), supplemented by a broader universe of eight private robotics firms and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression, using the $125M total raised as a proxy for implied post-money valuation, applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement to next stage, yielding $238M. Peer-median analysis across the three direct comparables produces $1.8B, with a tight range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The wide divergence between methods reflects structural uncertainty: stage-progression provides a floor based on capital deployed, while peer-median anchors to market multiples observed in contemporaneous fundings.

The triangulated analysis supports a range from $202M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $994M. The 10x spread between methods signals material uncertainty around market positioning relative to peers. Key variables include revenue scale and growth trajectory relative to Bedrock Robotics and Dexterity, technology differentiation, and customer concentration. A valuation toward the peer median ($1.8B) would imply Freeform commands comparable market positioning; substantial discount would require documented gaps in product-market fit or customer traction.
